target.description: Best-effort reconstruction of the visual behavior of a healthy period DMG reflective STN panel on a modern display

evidencePriority: contemporary measured STN data under comparable conditions

gradient.interpolation: piecewise linear light between adjacent sRGB states

aperture.basis: 70/80 proportion sampled from BGB's explicitly idealized close-up

temporal.classification: bounded DMG-drive and period-material STN physical reconstruction

physicalModel.runtimeState: normalized depth-average sin(theta)^2 director coordinate plus separate reflected-optical and ionic states
physicalModel.runtimeIntegrator: 65-bin generated director-drift LUT at the DMG 59.7275 Hz reference frame period

ws2Acceptance.reason: The normal Shader now integrates a generated director-drift field derived from the documented DMG drive, bounded period-STN material ensemble, Frank-Oseen/Ericksen-Leslie solver, and reflective Jones solver. Empirical endpoint times were removed from the normal path.
ws2Acceptance.completionStandard: The normal Shader must be a validated runtime reduction of the causal chain DMG row/column waveform -> pixel voltage -> STN director dynamics -> reflected spectral response.
requiredArtifacts: versioned DMG row/column waveform and four-shade voltage model
tested Frank-Oseen and declared Ericksen-Leslie director solver
tested Jones or Berreman reflective optical solver
generated LUT or modal Shader surrogate with approximation-error report
shared CPU, surrogate, GPU, and target-runtime validation

fitModel.role: interim empirical timing envelope; not the WS2 physical model
fitModel.runtimeEncoding: per-frame alpha values are exact encodings of continuous exponential rates at 59.7275 Hz

anchors.meaning: later improved low-viscosity and high-birefringence STN mixture
mean of turn-on and turn-off for a deliberately fast 4 um, 1/200-duty prototype at 20 C

legacyInterimBridge.classification: superseded empirical regression envelope retained only for output comparison
legacyInterimBridge.rationale: BGB constrains DMG-like persistence qualitatively; period STN literature supplies the aggregate scale and supports faster driven darkening than field-free clearing.

ionicModel.classification: separate literature-constrained slow mechanism; not used to create ordinary motion response

candidates.classification: bounded project bridge using the conventional-period aggregate anchor
candidates.rationale: Preserves the conventional 300 ms aggregate scale while keeping driven darkening faster than field-free clearing.

candidates.classification: historical fast-envelope diagnostic, not a DMG revision claim
candidates.rationale: Uses twice Okada's explicitly defined 80 ms mean ton/toff result as a 160 ms combined lower-envelope diagnostic; it does not assign the optimized prototype to the DMG.

candidates.classification: bounded slow-envelope project bridge, not a DMG revision claim
candidates.rationale: Applies a declared 1.5x slow-side scale around the conventional 300 ms anchor to expose uncertainty from material, temperature, and multiplex conditions.

scanout.classification: DMG-specific documented frame timing and captured CPL row latch

ws3Acceptance.completionStandard: The Shader must split previous and current physical drive at the captured CPL line-end event, preserve the WS2 one-step path for unchanged pixels, pass CPU causal tests, and compile and run on the KONKR target.
ws3Acceptance.result: The CPU report passes first/middle/last-row, same-row drive, cross-frame, unchanged, equilibrium, and no-scanout checks. The generated full target preset compiled on Mali Vulkan at exact 4x; a deterministic shade transition presented the expected top-before-middle-before-bottom row phase without changing settled row uniformity.

retention.classification: period-protocol and kinetic-literature constrained reconstruction with explicit optical bridge
retention.limits: No source identifies DMG adsorption/desorption rates or a residual-voltage-to-optical curve. Kinetics are reconstructed from the period 1994/1997 protocols plus a later direct kinetic measurement that satisfies the period release bound; optical gain remains an explicit low-amplitude project bridge.

spatial.classification: reference-image-matched aperture plus passive-matrix RMS selection loss and period-bounded distributed-RC spatial loading

crosstalkModel.classification: period-evidence-bounded electrical reconstruction; not a surviving-panel measurement

toneOrderGuard.classification: runtime safety boundary for a period-bounded model; not a Nintendo electrical parameter
toneOrderGuard.regressionPattern: shade 3 Tetris mino border with shade 2 interior

crosstalkModel.mechanism: one-ended row/column resistor ladders, pixel capacitance and leakage, comparable period driver output resistance, DMG three-dwell waveform, structure-preserving KCL common-electrode reduction without image-pattern coefficients, continuous WS2 voltage/director/optical coupling

ws6Acceptance.completionStandard: Periodic host-footprint integration must preserve aperture area and reflector-shadow gap energy at exact 4x/5x/6x, representative fractional scales, viewport offsets, edges, corners, and crops, then compile and agree in linear-light average at exact 4x and fractional 3.5x on KONKR.
ws6Acceptance.result: The corrected periodic aperture and active-shadow joint integrals preserve 0.765625 aperture area and 0.191875 shadow-gap area. CPU maximum error is 1e-12; KONKR 4x versus 3.5x presented linear RGB differs by at most 0.00144461 under a 0.002 tolerance.

ws5Acceptance.completionStandard: A versioned period-parameter record, distributed electrical solver, bounded ensemble, WS2 optical coupling, declared Shader approximation error, canonical pattern suite, constant-field invariant, and KONKR CPU/GPU/runtime receipt must all pass.
ws5Acceptance.result: The image-fitted directional kernel was rejected after a solid-pixel L-shaped artifact. Its replacement sums the distributed KCL equations and retains the common-electrode RC mode, with no image-pattern coefficients. A later mixed-tone Tetris regression exposed shade-specific uniform-baseline over-correction that saturated shade 2 interiors to shade 3. Runtime now bounds the uncertain correction to +/-0.125 shade, and the generated mixed-tone gate preserves at least 0.75 shade between shade 2 and shade 3. The five-pass Mali Vulkan path presents post-fix drive codes near 181 and 244 for the two dark tones and retains the distinction after pieces settle.

frontend.reason: The per-frame ionic increments are smaller than a reliable RGBA16F update over much of the state range.

targetRuntimeVerification.result: Normal-forward N=1 timing, precision, numeric settled-state output, motion pacing, save/load, pause, focus loss, and clean content close passed on the named target.
